text:
# Depth and Geometry Supervision

Also called: Geometric Regularization, Depth-Aware Training, Geometry Priors

## Overview
Depth and Geometry Supervision methods augment the standard [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md) in [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) training](#970-nerf-training-loop.md) with explicit [geometric constraints](#9270-geometry-and-surface-priors.md) derived from depth estimates or structural priors [S1, S5]. These methods solve the shape-radiance ambiguity and overfitting issues that arise in sparse-view or textureless scenarios by enforcing that the rendered density distribution aligns with known geometric structures [S1, S8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Unlike sibling methods that rely on semantic consistency [11955-semantic-consistency-loss-clip-based.md] or diffusion priors [7381-diffusion-regularized-nerf.md], this family explicitly minimizes the discrepancy between rendered depth/density and external depth maps, sparse point clouds, or internal geometric consistency metrics [S1, S5].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within the augmented loss structure defined by [Regularization and Loss Functions](8586-regularization-and-loss-functions.md), where the [total loss](#4177-total-loss-function.md) is $\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} + \sum_k \lambda_k \mathcal{L}_k$ [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. The geometric terms $\mathcal{L}_k$ typically involve the rendered expected depth $\hat{D}(\mathbf{r})$ or the ray termination distribution $h(t) = T(t)\sigma(t)$ [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. The rendered depth for a ray $\mathbf{r}$ is computed as the weighted average of sample distances $t_i$:
$$ \hat{D}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^N w_i t_i $$
where $w_i = T_i (1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i))$ are the rendering weights [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Gradients are backpropagated through this [differentiable rendering equation](#6839-reynolds-transport-theorem-for-differentiable-rendering.md) to update the density field $\sigma$ [S1, 8582-regnerf.md].

## Subtopics

### [Geometric Baseline Regularization](7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md)
A composite loss designed to prevent degenerate solutions (e.g., copying training images) in few-view settings without external depth data. It enforces foreground completeness, frustum consistency, and depth distribution compactness. Choose this when external depth priors are unavailable but geometric plausibility is required.

### [Guided Optimization of NeRF](7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md)
Mitigates shape-radiance ambiguity in indoor scenes by adaptively narrowing the ray sampling interval based on monocular depth priors refined by cross-view reprojection errors. Choose this for indoor scenes with texture-less regions where uniform sampling fails.

### [Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map](8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md)
Addresses single-view reconstruction by fusing multiple perspective depth maps into a canonical panorama depth map via deformable alignment before training. Choose this when only a single 360-degree panorama is available.

### [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md)
Accelerates convergence and improves quality in sparse-view settings by enforcing that the rendered ray termination distribution matches sparse 3D keypoints from Structure-from-Motion (SfM). Choose this when sparse SfM points are available and no dense depth is present.

### [Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md)
Enforces continuity on rendered depth maps using external priors (e.g., DepthAnythingV2) by penalizing local depth variations between neighbors using a KNN approach. Choose this when high-quality monocular depth estimates are available and sharp edges must be preserved.

### [Statistical Depth Refinement](10185-statistical-depth-refinement.md)
Mitigates noisy stereo depth supervision by dynamically replacing corrupt pixels (e.g., specular highlights) with smoother estimates from the model's early-stage underfitting output. Choose this when stereo depth is available but contains significant outliers.

### [Novel View Regularization](10806-novel-view-regularization.md)
Mitigates ambiguity in sparse data by injecting synthetic rays from virtual viewpoints to enforce geometric smoothness in the density field. Choose this to prevent floaters and overfitting without external depth data.

### [3D Point Supervision Loss](12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md)
Minimizes the distance between backprojected rendered depth points and ground-truth 3D points, enabling pose registration in sparse-view regimes. Choose this when 3D point clouds are available and pose refinement is needed.

### Coarse-Fine Consistency Loss
A loss function that enforces consistency between depth estimates of the coarse and fine [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) models to prevent ineffective hierarchical sampling and blur [S1].
$$ \mathcal{L}_{cfc} = \mathbf{1}_{\{m_f=1\}} \odot \|z_c - \hat{\nabla}(z_f)\|^2 + \mathbf{1}_{\{m_c=1\}} \odot \|\hat{\nabla}(z_c) - z_f\|^2 $$
where $z_c$ and $z_f$ are coarse and fine depths, and $m_c/m_f$ are reliability masks determined by reprojection [S1].

### Zero-level set projection
Refines inaccurate median depth from a pre-trained NeRF, particularly at grazing view angles, by iteratively projecting points onto the zero level-set of the surface using TSDF values [S2].
For each 3D point $p$ on the viewing ray, perform exactly 4 iterative gradient descent steps along the ray direction using the TSDF predicted value to update the point position [S2].
$$ p_{new} = p_{old} + \alpha \times \hat{t} $$
where $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}] = \phi(p)$; $p$ is the current 3D point, $\alpha$ is a small constant step size, and $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}]$ are the tangent, normal, and feature outputs from network $\phi$ evaluated at $p$ [S2].
Parameter: $\alpha$: Small constant controlling the step size of the gradient descent update. Value not specified in this section [S2].
Pitfall: Median depth from a pre-trained NeRF becomes inaccurate when the angle between the view direction and the surface is small (grazing angles) [S2].
Usage: Applied in NeRFMeshing as a preprocessing step to initialize the mesh geometry before training the SSAN model [S2].

### Robust Depth Loss
A loss function designed to address geometry error degradation in extrapolation performance by being less sensitive to outliers than [L2 loss](#6038-mean-square-error-mse.md), encouraging NeRF to terminate rays around pseudo depth while retaining freedom for inaccurate geometry [S3].
$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{robust}}(\mathbf{r}) = \begin{cases} 0.5\Delta D(\mathbf{r})^{2}, &\text{if } \Delta D(\mathbf{r}) < \beta \\ \beta^{2} (0.5 + \log (\frac{\Delta D(\mathbf{r})}{\beta})), &\text{otherwise } \end{cases} $$
where $\Delta D(\mathbf{r}) = \hat{D}(\mathbf{r}) - D(\mathbf{r})$ is the absolute depth difference, $\beta$ is a constant set to 0.1, and $\hat{D}(\mathbf{r})$ is the depth expectation along the camera axis of ray $r(t)$ [S3].
Parameter: $\beta$: A constant threshold for the robust [depth loss](#7487-pseudo-depth-supervised-loss.md), set to 0.1 throughout the experiments [S3].

### Depth Supervision with Planar Architectural Depth Priors
Incorporates precomputed depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls into NeRF training to enforce geometric constraints on textureless planar surfaces [S4].
Steps: 1. Compute depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls using semantic segmentation. 2. Incorporate these priors into training with MSE and BoundL losses alongside photometric loss. 3. Train until convergence [S4].
Parameter: $\delta$ (BoundL tolerance): 1 mm. $\lambda_{color}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room). $\lambda_{depth}$: 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room) [S4].
Number: [RMSE](#10453-depth-accuracy-metrics.md) of priors vs ground truth: 2.786 mm (bedroom), 3.201 mm (living room). Converged in 120,000 iterations [S4].
Comparison: Faster convergence than photometric-only (120k vs 200k) and patch-regularization (120k vs 280k) methods due to depth supervision enabling quick identification of empty spaces, concentrating sampling on occupied regions, and providing a stronger optimization signal [S4].

### Indirect Depth Supervision (KL Loss)
A regularization technique that uses depth priors to constrain the NeRF weights by aligning the probability distribution of rendering weights with the [depth prior](#7616-depth-regularization.md), specifically using KL divergence [S5].
$$ L_{KL} = \sum_{i}^{N_r} \sum_{t=t_n}^{t_f} D(r_i) - \epsilon \log w_k \exp(-\frac{(t - D(r_i))^2}{2\hat{\sigma}^2}) \Delta t_k $$
where $w_k$ are rendering weights, $t_k$ are sampled points, $\Delta t_k$ are distances, $D(r_i)$ is ground truth depth, $\epsilon$ is a kernel parameter, and $\hat{\sigma}$ is a variance parameter [S5].
Parameter: $\epsilon(x)$: A kernel that integrates to one (a distribution) with a bounded domain parameterized by $\epsilon$ [S5].
Pitfall: The URF loss (Urban-NeRF) has no open-source implementation, so KL loss is selected as the representative for indirect supervision [S5].

### Geometry and Opacity Regularization
[Sparsity loss](#1203-nerf-training-configuration.md): $L_S = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} O(i)$, where $N$ is number of rays intersecting the 3D box, encouraging sparse opacity to suppress floaters [S6].
Opacity loss: $L_O = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} [O(i) \cdot \log(O(i)) + (1 - O(i)) \cdot \log(1 - O(i))]$, encouraging opacity values to be 0 or 1 to avoid translucent effects [S6].

### Depth Filtering with RGB Confidence
Filters predicted depth maps by computing a per-pixel confidence metric based on the reconstruction error between predicted and ground truth RGB images [S7, unofficial].
Steps: Load predicted RGBs and depths from NeRF results directory. Load ground truth RGBs from the data directory. Compute confidence map by taking 1 minus the mean absolute error between normalized predicted and ground truth RGBs across channels. Pass ground truth RGB, predicted depth, confidence map, and save path to a parallel processing pool for filtering [S7, unofficial].
Parameter: worker_num: Number of parallel workers for the multiprocessing pool, default 8 [S7, unofficial].

### Direct Depth Supervision
A training objective that directly compares the depth rendered by the NeRF with a ground truth depth prior using a pixel-wise loss function [S5].
Steps: First sample a batch of $N_r$ rays, then compare the rendered depth and ground truth depth with different loss functions (MSE or L1) [S5].

### GeoAug
An approach that uses data augmentation by rendering new training images with new noisy camera poses using DSNeRF as a baseline and using depth as regularization [S8].

## Background
The concept of using depth priors to regularize NeRF optimization originated with the recognition that photometric loss alone is insufficient for sparse-view reconstruction, leading to "floaters" and shape-radiance ambiguity [S1, S5]. Early work like DS-NeRF introduced sparse [3D point supervision](#12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md) to guide the density field [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Subsequent methods expanded this to dense monocular depth priors [S1, 9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md], stereo depth with statistical refinement [S1, 10185-statistical-depth-refinement.md], and architectural priors for indoor scenes [S4]. The family has evolved to include indirect supervision via KL divergence [S5, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md] and consistency losses between [coarse-fine sampling](#8172-coarse-fine-sampling.md) stages [S1, Coarse-Fine Consistency Loss]. It is widely used in applications requiring high geometric fidelity from limited views, such as autonomous navigation, architectural modeling, and novel view synthesis for VR [S1, S2, S4, S6].
